name: Beyond Chat: 8 Core User Intents Driving AI Interaction
tagline: Intent-first framework for choosing the right workflow, interface, and success measure for an AI feature
description:
Taras Bakusevych maps AI interaction into eight user intents: learn, create, delegate, oversee, monitor, find and explore, play, and connect. Each intent gets its own goal, workflow, interface patterns, failure modes, and success measure.

The article also defines six behavior settings that product teams can tune separately: personalization, initiative, autonomy, tone, transparency, and risk appetite. It gives teams a practical way to move beyond chat as the default AI interface.
pricing_detail: Free public article on Syntax Stream. No account was required when checked on 2026-09-10.
agent_guidance: Use this before choosing the interface for an AI feature. Identify the primary intent, define its success measure, and select a surface that supports the workflow. Do not start with chat by default. Use the six behavior settings to make initiative, autonomy, transparency, tone, personalization, and risk explicit.
why_it_matters: It turns a broad request for an AI feature into a clear product decision: what the user wants to do, which interface supports it, and how the team will measure success.
tier_reason: The framework is clear, broad, and directly applicable to product design. It stays a practitioner taxonomy rather than a formal standard, which keeps it below the strongest primary research.
notable_for: one success measure for each intent
six behavior settings for AI features
evidence: https://syntaxstream.substack.com/p/beyond-chat-8-core-user-intents-driving returned 200. The public article is by Taras Bakusevych and is dated 2026-01-12. It defines eight intents: learn, create, delegate, oversee, monitor, find and explore, play, and connect. It also defines personalization, initiative, autonomy, tone, transparency, and risk appetite as behavior settings. Checked 2026-09-10.

name: 39 Principles for Designing Human-AI Interaction
tagline: Applied principles for building AI interfaces with clear evidence, user control, recoverable failure, and bounded autonomy
description:
Taras Bakusevych turns research on human-AI interaction, mixed-initiative systems, trust in automation, and responsible AI into 39 product principles. The framework covers probabilistic foundations, expectation setting, calibrated trust, transparency, control and agency, graceful failure, co-creation, responsible autonomy, and sustained reliance.

Use it as a design review for the full AI interaction cycle. It covers what the system should explain, when it should ask or act, how users check output, and how they recover when the system is wrong.
pricing_detail: Free public article on Syntax Stream. No account was required when checked on 2026-09-10.
agent_guidance: Use this as a product review before development or release. Check whether the interface shows its AI role, sources, limits, plan, and important state changes. Make acceptance, correction, rejection, undo, and escalation easy. Increase approval and review requirements as actions become less reversible or more consequential.
why_it_matters: It connects established human-AI research to interface decisions that a product team can inspect in a design review.
tier_reason: The article connects established research and current model guidance to a detailed product review framework. The live title now says 39 principles, despite the older URL slug.
notable_for: autonomy tied to stakes and reversibility
design for model and data changes
evidence: https://syntaxstream.substack.com/p/42-principles-for-designing-humanai returned 200. The live page is dated 2026-06-30 and now presents 39 numbered principles, although the URL slug still says 42. The framework cites mixed-initiative interaction, the Google PAIR Guidebook, IBM generative AI principles, Microsoft human-AI guidelines, and current model guidance. Checked 2026-09-10.
